text:
maya: kicking off a 2-week burndown for the GPU headroom postmortem followups. Goal: close the top 6 action items that keep recurring (quota spikes, scheduler churn, KV cache misses). I sketched owners below — please ack & add timing.

maya: TL;DR action owners I propose:
- Samir: scheduler tuning + safe defaults (prototype + canary)
- Elena: quota policy adjustments + quota backstop rules
- Jay: headroom forecasting + burst plan (tooling + dashboard)
- Maya: cross-cutting followups + weekly rollup

samir: ack. I'll start with tuning the bin-packing thresholds and preemption window. Plan: run A/B on a small pool by EOD Thu, roll to canary next week.

elena: ack. I'll add strict quota backstop for low-priority jobs and a soft cap for experimental workloads. Need input: what % headroom should we reserve for critical SLO traffic? @maya

maya: thinking 15% target headroom for peak 99th latency use cases. If autoscale can reliably add within 90s we could drop to 10% but let's be conservative for now.

jay: ack. I'll wire up a quick baseline: 3x historical 95th, 95th->99th delta, and a burst multiplier. Will put a dashboard tile and an alert if predicted headroom < 20% for next 30m.

ops-bot: New ticket created: INF-3742 "Scheduler tuning: conservative defaults and canary" assigned -> samir. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3742 :robot_face:

maya: nice. Please include rollback steps in the ticket. Also add short eval prompts to catch quality regressions if we change batching.

samir: will do. Quick config snippet I'll test (pushed to sandbox):
```
# tuned scheduler defaults
bin_pack_threshold: 0.78
preemption_window_s: 45
burst_reserve_ratio: 0.15
```

elena: FYI quota backstop prototype: adding a per-customer throttle bucket and emergency override for SRE. Draft policy: throttle experimental teams at 60% of reserved quota, notify owners at 70%, hard cap at 95%.

jay: a couple follow-ups from the postmortem patterns: 1) repeated small spikes from background embedding jobs at midnight, 2) model version rollouts causing transient KV cache thrash. I'll add scheduled shard warming for rollouts.

sre-oncall: from oncall perspective, we need a single runbook section: "capacity shortfall -> attempt add nodes -> if unavailable, route to backup model variant -> notify CS". I'll draft and link.

maya: action checklist and timeline (2-week sprint):
- Week 0 (this week): propose configs + tickets (owners assigned)
- Week 1: canary changes (scheduler + quota) + headroom tile up
- Week 2: roll to prod + validation, run synthetic load, close items

samir: estimated effort: 2 engineer-days for canary + 1 day for rollback docs.

elena: 1.5 engineer-days for quota prototype + policy review with security.

jay: 2 engineer-days for forecasting pipeline + dashboard.

maya: ok. Owners, please set due dates in the tickets: target completion by 3620000000 + 14 days (set in Jira). I'll run the weekly rollup on Monday standup.

samir: quick question — for the canary do we use dedicated small pool or tagging? I prefer small dedicated pool to avoid cross-traffic.

maya: dedicate a 4-GPU pool labeled "sched-canary-1" and limit traffic to internal teams. Good call.

elena: added a doc link to quota policy draft: https://docs.redwood.com/ops/quota-backstop-draft (please comment).

ops-bot: Reminder: recurring reminder created -> "GPU headroom burndown sync" every Mon 09:30 starting next week.

jay: I'll post the headroom forecast chart in #eng-platform when the tile is ready.

sre-oncall: I'll convert the runbook section into a short checklist and add it to the incident playbook page.

maya: thanks everyone. If anyone needs help splitting tasks or getting infra creds for the canary pool ping me directly. Let's try to avoid repeating the same action items next quarter. :thumbsup:

samir: acked :+1:

elena: acked :rocket:

jay: acked :ok_hand:

maya: closing thread here — will post weekly burndown updates as comments.
